title: Chat SDK agents can now stream generative UI with json-render
description: You can now stream generative UI from your Chat SDK agent with json-render . With a typed catalog of components, the agent writes a JSON spec that json-render converts into a Chat SDK card. Each adapter then posts the card in its platform’s native format, such as Block Kit on Slack and Adaptive Cards on Teams. The catalog covers tables, charts, buttons, and more, so there’s no separate tool to build and maintain for each message shape. Stream cards as the model writes streamCard posts the card once its root element has content and updates the message as new elements stream in. Edits go out at most once every 500 ms by default, which matches Chat SDK’s streaming interval. Once the stream ends, the message shows the final, validated card. Validate specs and enforce platform limits toCard checks every element’s props against its component schema and throws CardSpecError for an invalid spec. Each problem gets its own readable issue, so you can send the list back to the model for a corrected spec. Platforms cap what a single message can hold, and Chat SDK adapters degrade content past those caps. The Slack adapter, for example, turns a second table into a code block. Pass limits to reject those specs instead. Read the documentation to get started, or try the playground . Read more

title: AI Gateway adds DeepSeek Search and Fetch tools
description: DeepSeek Search and DeepSeek Fetch are now available through AI Gateway . Search finds relevant pages with titles, URLs, and summaries. Fetch retrieves page content as Markdown for your model to read. Use both tools with any model that supports tool calling, using one AI Gateway API key. No separate DeepSeek account is required, and you can keep the same tools when switching model providers. These helpers are available in AI SDK 6.0.321 and later on v6, or 7.0.160 and later on v7. Update with pnpm add ai@latest and set your AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY . To combine search and page retrieval, pass both helpers in tools : You can also use alternative search tools with DeepSeek Fetch if DeepSeek Search fails: Search fallback is model-directed, so provider order and retry limits are best effort. DeepSeek Fetch can retrieve a result URL from any of these search tools. Search and Fetch each cost $0.75 per 1,000 billable requests. Failed requests, timeouts, and empty results have no tool charge. Model tokens are billed separately. See the DeepSeek Search documentation and DeepSeek Fetch documentation for configuration options and pricing details. AI Gateway provides one API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring routing, retries, and failover. You can use an AI Gateway API key or bring your own provider key . Read more

title: Vercel CLI can now set new projects to expire
description: You can now set a new project to expire when you deploy it with Vercel CLI . Expired projects are deleted automatically, so prototypes, demos, and test apps don't need cleaning up by hand. Run vercel deploy with --delete-project-after and a duration: Supported durations are 1h , 1d , 1w , 2w , and 30d , and the CLI prints the date and time when the project expires. The flag only applies when vercel deploy creates the project. If you deploy to an existing project with the flag, its expiration doesn't change and the CLI prints a warning. To remove a project's expiration, run vercel project keep : Update Vercel CLI to v65.12.0 or later to get started. Learn more in the vercel deploy documentation . Read more

title: Vercel Tracing is now generally available
description: Vercel Tracing is now generally available on all plans. You can now search and inspect traces from the dashboard or the Vercel CLI , and new Next.js projects get tracing by default. Pricing is unchanged from the beta. Browse and search traces in the dashboard In beta, you could only open a trace per request from the Logs page. The new Traces page shows every trace and span in one place, for a project or your whole team. Switch between a Spans list and a Traces list, filter each, and search with Kibana Query Language (KQL). A Live mode streams new traces as they arrive. A query like span.name:db* AND span.duration > 500 narrows to slow database spans by name and duration. Search traces from the CLI The Traces page uses the same KQL as vercel traces search --query , so a query built in the dashboard runs in the CLI unchanged. Search covers every project in your team, or one project with the --project flag. Inspect a single trace with vercel traces inspect <request-id> , and manage a project's sampling rules with vercel traces config . Automatic tracing for new Next.js projects In beta, nothing was collected until you added a sampling rule. Starting with Next.js 16.5, new projects created on Vercel that include at least one Node.js function get tracing turned on after their first successful build. Vercel adds one sampling rule tracing 100% of requests in all environments and injects instrumentation at build time, so traces include Next.js framework spans with no setup. To opt out, remove all sampling rules in Settings → Tracing. Longer retention In beta, traces followed your runtime log retention. Hobby now keeps traces for 3 days instead of 1 hour, Pro for 14 days instead of 1 day, and Enterprise for 14 days instead of 3 days. Read the Tracing documentation to learn more. Read more
